The Free Performance Lunch

There�s an interesting phenomenon that�s known as �Andy giveth, and Bill taketh away.� No matter how fast processors get, software consistently finds new ways to eat up the extra speed. Make a CPU ten times as fast, and software will usually find ten times as much to do (or, in some cases, will feel at liberty to do it ten times less efficiently). Most classes of applications have enjoyed free and regular performance gains for several decades, even without releasing new versions or doing anything special, because the CPU manufacturers (primarily) and memory and disk manufacturers (secondarily) have reliably enabled ever-newer and ever-faster mainstream systems. Clock speed isn�t the only measure of performance, or even necessarily a good one, but it�s an instructive one: We�re used to seeing 500MHz CPUs give way to 1GHz CPUs give way to 2GHz CPUs, and so on. Today we�re in the 3GHz range on mainstream computers.

The key question is: When will it end? After all, Moore�s Law predicts exponential growth, and clearly exponential growth can�t continue forever before we reach hard physical limits; light isn�t getting any faster. The growth must eventually slow down and even end. (Caveat: Yes, Moore�s Law applies principally to transistor densities, but the same kind of exponential growth has occurred in related areas such as clock speeds. There�s even faster growth in other spaces, most notably the data storage explosion, but that important trend belongs in a different article.)

If you�re a software developer, chances are that you have already been riding the �free lunch� wave of desktop computer performance. Is your application�s performance borderline for some local operations? �Not to worry,� the conventional (if suspect) wisdom goes; �tomorrow�s processors will have even more throughput, and anyway today�s applications are increasingly throttled by factors other than CPU throughput and memory speed (e.g., they�re often I/O-bound, network-bound, database-bound).� Right?

Right enough, in the past. But dead wrong for the foreseeable future.

The good news is that processors are going to continue to become more powerful. The bad news is that, at least in the short term, the growth will come mostly in directions that do not take most current applications along for their customary free ride.

Over the past 30 years, CPU designers have achieved performance gains in three main areas, the first two of which focus on straight-line execution flow:

clock speed

execution optimization

cache

Increasing clock speed is about getting more cycles. Running the CPU faster more or less directly means doing the same work faster.

Optimizing execution flow is about doing more work per cycle. Today�s CPUs sport some more powerful instructions, and they perform optimizations that range from the pedestrian to the exotic, including pipelining, branch prediction, executing multiple instructions in the same clock cycle(s), and even reordering the instruction stream for out-of-order execution. These techniques are all designed to make the instructions flow better and/or execute faster, and to squeeze the most work out of each clock cycle by reducing latency and maximizing the work accomplished per clock cycle.

Chip designers are under so much pressure to deliver ever-faster CPUs that they�ll risk changing the meaning of your program, and possibly break it, in order to make it run faster

Brief aside on instruction reordering and memory models: Note that some of what I just called �optimizations� are actually far more than optimizations, in that they can change the meaning of programs and cause visible effects that can break reasonable programmer expectations. This is significant. CPU designers are generally sane and well-adjusted folks who normally wouldn�t hurt a fly, and wouldn�t think of hurting your code� normally. But in recent years they have been willing to pursue aggressive optimizations just to wring yet more speed out of each cycle, even knowing full well that these aggressive rearrangements could endanger the semantics of your code. Is this Mr. Hyde making an appearance? Not at all. That willingness is simply a clear indicator of the extreme pressure the chip designers face to deliver ever-faster CPUs; they�re under so much pressure that they�ll risk changing the meaning of your program, and possibly break it, in order to make it run faster. Two noteworthy examples in this respect are write reordering and read reordering: Allowing a processor to reorder write operations has consequences that are so surprising, and break so many programmer expectations, that the feature generally has to be turned off because it�s too difficult for programmers to reason correctly about the meaning of their programs in the presence of arbitrary write reordering. Reordering read operations can also yield surprising visible effects, but that is more commonly left enabled anyway because it isn�t quite as hard on programmers, and the demands for performance cause designers of operating systems and operating environments to compromise and choose models that place a greater burden on programmers because that is viewed as a lesser evil than giving up the optimization opportunities.

Finally, increasing the size of on-chip cache is about staying away from RAM. Main memory continues to be so much slower than the CPU that it makes sense to put the data closer to the processor�and you can�t get much closer than being right on the die. On-die cache sizes have soared, and today most major chip vendors will sell you CPUs that have 2MB and more of on-board L2 cache. (Of these three major historical approaches to boosting CPU performance, increasing cache is the only one that will continue in the near term. I�ll talk a little more about the importance of cache later on.)

Okay. So what does this mean?

A fundamentally important thing to recognize about this list is that all of these areas are concurrency-agnostic. Speedups in any of these areas will directly lead to speedups in sequential (nonparallel, single-threaded, single-process) applications, as well as applications that do make use of concurrency. That�s important, because the vast majority of today�s applications are single-threaded, for good reasons that I�ll get into further below.

Of course, compilers have had to keep up; sometimes you need to recompile your application, and target a specific minimum level of CPU, in order to benefit from new instructions (e.g., MMX, SSE) and some new CPU features and characteristics. But, by and large, even old applications have always run significantly faster�even without being recompiled to take advantage of all the new instructions and features offered by the latest CPUs.

That world was a nice place to be. Unfortunately, it has already disappeared.

Obstacles, and Why You Don�t Have 10GHz Today

CPU performance growth as we have known it hit a wall two years ago. Most people have only recently started to notice.

You can get similar graphs for other chips, but I�m going to use Intel data here. Figure 1 graphs the history of Intel chip introductions by clock speed and number of transistors. The number of transistors continues to climb, at least for now. Clock speed, however, is a different story.

Figure 1: Intel CPU Introductions (graph updated August 2009; article text original from December 2004)

Around the beginning of 2003, you�ll note a disturbing sharp turn in the previous trend toward ever-faster CPU clock speeds. I�ve added lines to show the limit trends in maximum clock speed; instead of continuing on the previous path, as indicated by the thin dotted line, there is a sharp flattening. It has become harder and harder to exploit higher clock speeds due to not just one but several physical issues, notably heat (too much of it and too hard to dissipate), power consumption (too high), and current leakage problems.

Quick: What�s the clock speed on the CPU(s) in your current workstation? Are you running at 10GHz? On Intel chips, we reached 2GHz a long time ago (August 2001), and according to CPU trends before 2003, now in early 2005 we should have the first 10GHz Pentium-family chips. A quick look around shows that, well, actually, we don�t. What�s more, such chips are not even on the horizon�we have no good idea at all about when we might see them appear.

Well, then, what about 4GHz? We�re at 3.4GHz already�surely 4GHz can�t be far away? Alas, even 4GHz seems to be remote indeed. In mid-2004, as you probably know, Intel first delayed its planned introduction of a 4GHz chip until 2005, and then in fall 2004 it officially abandoned its 4GHz plans entirely. As of this writing, Intel is planning to ramp up a little further to 3.73GHz in early 2005 (already included in Figure 1 as the upper-right-most dot), but the clock race really is over, at least for now; Intel�s and most processor vendors� future lies elsewhere as chip companies aggressively pursue the same new multicore directions.

We�ll probably see 4GHz CPUs in our mainstream desktop machines someday, but it won�t be in 2005. Sure, Intel has samples of their chips running at even higher speeds in the lab�but only by heroic efforts, such as attaching hideously impractical quantities of cooling equipment. You won�t have that kind of cooling hardware in your office any day soon, let alone on your lap while computing on the plane.

TANSTAAFL: Moore�s Law and the Next Generation(s)

�There ain�t no such thing as a free lunch.� �R. A. Heinlein, The Moon Is a Harsh Mistress

Does this mean Moore�s Law is over? Interestingly, the answer in general seems to be no. Of course, like all exponential progressions, Moore�s Law must end someday, but it does not seem to be in danger for a few more years yet. Despite the wall that chip engineers have hit in juicing up raw clock cycles, transistor counts continue to explode and it seems CPUs will continue to follow Moore�s Law-like throughput gains for some years to come.

Myths and Realities: 2 x 3GHz < 6 GHz

So a dual-core CPU that combines two 3GHz cores practically offers 6GHz of processing power. Right?

Wrong. Even having two threads running on two physical processors doesn�t mean getting two times the performance. Similarly, most multi-threaded applications won�t run twice as fast on a dual-core box. They should run faster than on a single-core CPU; the performance gain just isn�t linear, that�s all.

Why not? First, there is coordination overhead between the cores to ensure cache coherency (a consistent view of cache, and of main memory) and to perform other handshaking. Today, a two- or four-processor machine isn�t really two or four times as fast as a single CPU even for multi-threaded applications. The problem remains essentially the same even when the CPUs in question sit on the same die.

Second, unless the two cores are running different processes, or different threads of a single process that are well-written to run independently and almost never wait for each other, they won�t be well utilized. (Despite this, I will speculate that today�s single-threaded applications as actually used in the field could actually see a performance boost for most users by going to a dual-core chip, not because the extra core is actually doing anything useful, but because it is running the adware and spyware that infest many users� systems and are otherwise slowing down the single CPU that user has today. I leave it up to you to decide whether adding a CPU to run your spyware is the best solution to that problem.)

If you�re running a single-threaded application, then the application can only make use of one core. There should be some speedup as the operating system and the application can run on separate cores, but typically the OS isn�t going to be maxing out the CPU anyway so one of the cores will be mostly idle. (Again, the spyware can share the OS�s core most of the time.)

The key difference, which is the heart of this article, is that the performance gains are going to be accomplished in fundamentally different ways for at least the next couple of processor generations. And most current applications will no longer benefit from the free ride without significant redesign.

For the near-term future, meaning for the next few years, the performance gains in new chips will be fueled by three main approaches, only one of which is the same as in the past. The near-term future performance growth drivers are:

hyperthreading

multicore

cache

Hyperthreading is about running two or more threads in parallel inside a single CPU. Hyperthreaded CPUs are already available today, and they do allow some instructions to run in parallel. A limiting factor, however, is that although a hyper-threaded CPU has some extra hardware including extra registers, it still has just one cache, one integer math unit, one FPU, and in general just one each of most basic CPU features. Hyperthreading is sometimes cited as offering a 5% to 15% performance boost for reasonably well-written multi-threaded applications, or even as much as 40% under ideal conditions for carefully written multi-threaded applications. That�s good, but it�s hardly double, and it doesn�t help single-threaded applications.

Multicore is about running two or more actual CPUs on one chip. Some chips, including Sparc and PowerPC, have multicore versions available already. The initial Intel and AMD designs, both due in 2005, vary in their level of integration but are functionally similar. AMD�s seems to have some initial performance design advantages, such as better integration of support functions on the same die, whereas Intel�s initial entry basically just glues together two Xeons on a single die. The performance gains should initially be about the same as having a true dual-CPU system (only the system will be cheaper because the motherboard doesn�t have to have two sockets and associated �glue� chippery), which means something less than double the speed even in the ideal case, and just like today it will boost reasonably well-written multi-threaded applications. Not single-threaded ones.

Finally, on-die cache sizes can be expected to continue to grow, at least in the near term. Of these three areas, only this one will broadly benefit most existing applications. The continuing growth in on-die cache sizes is an incredibly important and highly applicable benefit for many applications, simply because space is speed. Accessing main memory is expensive, and you really don�t want to touch RAM if you can help it. On today�s systems, a cache miss that goes out to main memory often costs 10 to 50 times as much getting the information from the cache; this, incidentally, continues to surprise people because we all think of memory as fast, and it is fast compared to disks and networks, but not compared to on-board cache which runs at faster speeds. If an application�s working set fits into cache, we�re golden, and if it doesn�t, we�re not. That is why increased cache sizes will save some existing applications and breathe life into them for a few more years without requiring significant redesign: As existing applications manipulate more and more data, and as they are incrementally updated to include more code for new features, performance-sensitive operations need to continue to fit into cache. As the Depression-era old-timers will be quick to remind you, �Cache is king.�

(Aside: Here�s an anecdote to demonstrate �space is speed� that recently hit my compiler team. The compiler uses the same source base for the 32-bit and 64-bit compilers; the code is just compiled as either a 32-bit process or a 64-bit one. The 64-bit compiler gained a great deal of baseline performance by running on a 64-bit CPU, principally because the 64-bit CPU had many more registers to work with and had other code performance features. All well and good. But what about data? Going to 64 bits didn�t change the size of most of the data in memory, except that of course pointers in particular were now twice the size they were before. As it happens, our compiler uses pointers much more heavily in its internal data structures than most other kinds of applications ever would. Because pointers were now 8 bytes instead of 4 bytes, a pure data size increase, we saw a significant increase in the 64-bit compiler�s working set. That bigger working set caused a performance penalty that almost exactly offset the code execution performance increase we�d gained from going to the faster processor with more registers. As of this writing, the 64-bit compiler runs at the same speed as the 32-bit compiler, even though the source base is the same for both and the 64-bit processor offers better raw processing throughput. Space is speed.)

But cache is it. Hyperthreading and multicore CPUs will have nearly no impact on most current applications.

So what does this change in the hardware mean for the way we write software? By now you�ve probably noticed the basic answer, so let�s consider it and its consequences.

What This Means For Software: The Next Revolution

In the 1990s, we learned to grok objects. The revolution in mainstream software development from structured programming to object-oriented programming was the greatest such change in the past 20 years, and arguably in the past 30 years. There have been other changes, including the most recent (and genuinely interesting) naissance of web services, but nothing that most of us have seen during our careers has been as fundamental and as far-reaching a change in the way we write software as the object revolution.

Until now.

Starting today, the performance lunch isn�t free any more. Sure, there will continue to be generally applicable performance gains that everyone can pick up, thanks mainly to cache size improvements. But if you want your application to benefit from the continued exponential throughput advances in new processors, it will need to be a well-written concurrent (usually multithreaded) application. And that�s easier said than done, because not all problems are inherently parallelizable and because concurrent programming is hard.

I can hear the howls of protest: �Concurrency? That�s not news! People are already writing concurrent applications.� That�s true. Of a small fraction of developers.

Remember that people have been doing object-oriented programming since at least the days of Simula in the late 1960s. But OO didn�t become a revolution, and dominant in the mainstream, until the 1990s. Why then? The reason the revolution happened was primarily that our industry was driven by requirements to write larger and larger systems that solved larger and larger problems and exploited the greater and greater CPU and storage resources that were becoming available. OOP�s strengths in abstraction and dependency management made it a necessity for achieving large-scale software development that is economical, reliable, and repeatable.

Concurrency is the next major revolution in how we write software

Similarly, we�ve been doing concurrent programming since those same dark ages, writing coroutines and monitors and similar jazzy stuff. And for the past decade or so we�ve witnessed incrementally more and more programmers writing concurrent (multi-threaded, multi-process) systems. But an actual revolution marked by a major turning point toward concurrency has been slow to materialize. Today the vast majority of applications are single-threaded, and for good reasons that I�ll summarize in the next section.

By the way, on the matter of hype: People have always been quick to announce �the next software development revolution,� usually about their own brand-new technology. Don�t believe it. New technologies are often genuinely interesting and sometimes beneficial, but the biggest revolutions in the way we write software generally come from technologies that have already been around for some years and have already experienced gradual growth before they transition to explosive growth. This is necessary: You can only base a software development revolution on a technology that�s mature enough to build on (including having solid vendor and tool support), and it generally takes any new software technology at least seven years before it�s solid enough to be broadly usable without performance cliffs and other gotchas. As a result, true software development revolutions like OO happen around technologies that have already been undergoing refinement for years, often decades. Even in Hollywood, most genuine �overnight successes� have really been performing for many years before their big break.

Concurrency is the next major revolution in how we write software. Different experts still have different opinions on whether it will be bigger than OO, but that kind of conversation is best left to pundits. For technologists, the interesting thing is that concurrency is of the same order as OO both in the (expected) scale of the revolution and in the complexity and learning curve of the technology.

Benefits and Costs of Concurrency

There are two major reasons for which concurrency, especially multithreading, is already used in mainstream software. The first is to logically separate naturally independent control flows; for example, in a database replication server I designed it was natural to put each replication session on its own thread, because each session worked completely independently of any others that might be active (as long as they weren�t working on the same database row). The second and less common reason to write concurrent code in the past has been for performance, either to scalably take advantage of multiple physical CPUs or to easily take advantage of latency in other parts of the application; in my database replication server, this factor applied as well and the separate threads were able to scale well on multiple CPUs as our server handled more and more concurrent replication sessions with many other servers.

There are, however, real costs to concurrency. Some of the obvious costs are actually relatively unimportant. For example, yes, locks can be expensive to acquire, but when used judiciously and properly you gain much more from the concurrent execution than you lose on the synchronization, if you can find a sensible way to parallelize the operation and minimize or eliminate shared state.

Perhaps the second-greatest cost of concurrency is that not all applications are amenable to parallelization. I�ll say more about this later on.

Probably the greatest cost of concurrency is that concurrency really is hard: The programming model, meaning the model in the programmer�s head that he needs to reason reliably about his program, is much harder than it is for sequential control flow.

Everybody who learns concurrency thinks they understand it, ends up finding mysterious races they thought weren�t possible, and discovers that they didn�t actually understand it yet after all. As the developer learns to reason about concurrency, they find that usually those races can be caught by reasonable in-house testing, and they reach a new plateau of knowledge and comfort. What usually doesn�t get caught in testing, however, except in shops that understand why and how to do real stress testing, is those latent concurrency bugs that surface only on true multiprocessor systems, where the threads aren�t just being switched around on a single processor but where they really do execute truly simultaneously and thus expose new classes of errors. This is the next jolt for people who thought that surely now they know how to write concurrent code: I�ve come across many teams whose application worked fine even under heavy and extended stress testing, and ran perfectly at many customer sites, until the day that a customer actually had a real multiprocessor machine and then deeply mysterious races and corruptions started to manifest intermittently. In the context of today�s CPU landscape, then, redesigning your application to run multithreaded on a multicore machine is a little like learning to swim by jumping into the deep end�going straight to the least forgiving, truly parallel environment that is most likely to expose the things you got wrong. Even when you have a team that can reliably write safe concurrent code, there are other pitfalls; for example, concurrent code that is completely safe but isn�t any faster than it was on a single-core machine, typically because the threads aren�t independent enough and share a dependency on a single resource which re-serializes the program�s execution. This stuff gets pretty subtle.

The vast majority of programmers today don�t grok concurrency, just as the vast majority of programmers 15 years ago didn�t yet grok objects

Just as it is a leap for a structured programmer to learn OO (what�s an object? what�s a virtual function? how should I use inheritance? and beyond the �whats� and �hows,� why are the correct design practices actually correct?), it�s a leap of about the same magnitude for a sequential programmer to learn concurrency (what�s a race? what�s a deadlock? how can it come up, and how do I avoid it? what constructs actually serialize the program that I thought was parallel? how is the message queue my friend? and beyond the �whats� and �hows,� why are the correct design practices actually correct?).

The vast majority of programmers today don�t grok concurrency, just as the vast majority of programmers 15 years ago didn�t yet grok objects. But the concurrent programming model is learnable, particularly if we stick to message- and lock-based programming, and once grokked it isn�t that much harder than OO and hopefully can become just as natural. Just be ready and allow for the investment in training and time, for you and for your team.

(I deliberately limit the above to message- and lock-based concurrent programming models. There is also lock-free programming, supported most directly at the language level in Java 5 and in at least one popular C++ compiler. But concurrent lock-free programming is known to be very much harder for programmers to understand and reason about than even concurrent lock-based programming. Most of the time, only systems and library writers should have to understand lock-free programming, although virtually everybody should be able to take advantage of the lock-free systems and libraries those people produce. Frankly, even lock-based programming is hazardous.)

What It Means For Us

Okay, back to what it means for us.

1. The clear primary consequence we�ve already covered is that applications will increasingly need to be concurrent if they want to fully exploit CPU throughput gains that have now started becoming available and will continue to materialize over the next several years. For example, Intel is talking about someday producing 100-core chips; a single-threaded application can exploit at most 1/100 of such a chip�s potential throughput. �Oh, performance doesn�t matter so much, computers just keep getting faster� has always been a na�ve statement to be viewed with suspicion, and for the near future it will almost always be simply wrong.

Applications will increasingly need to be concurrent if they want to fully exploit continuing exponential CPU throughput gains

Efficiency and performance optimization will get more, not less, important

Now, not all applications (or, more precisely, important operations of an application) are amenable to parallelization. True, some problems, such as compilation, are almost ideally parallelizable. But others aren�t; the usual counterexample here is that just because it takes one woman nine months to produce a baby doesn�t imply that nine women could produce one baby in one month. You�ve probably come across that analogy before. But did you notice the problem with leaving the analogy at that? Here�s the trick question to ask the next person who uses it on you: Can you conclude from this that the Human Baby Problem is inherently not amenable to parallelization? Usually people relating this analogy err in quickly concluding that it demonstrates an inherently nonparallel problem, but that�s actually not necessarily correct at all. It is indeed an inherently nonparallel problem if the goal is to produce one child. It is actually an ideally parallelizable problem if the goal is to produce many children! Knowing the real goals can make all the difference. This basic goal-oriented principle is something to keep in mind when considering whether and how to parallelize your software.

2. Perhaps a less obvious consequence is that applications are likely to become increasingly CPU-bound. Of course, not every application operation will be CPU-bound, and even those that will be affected won�t become CPU-bound overnight if they aren�t already, but we seem to have reached the end of the �applications are increasingly I/O-bound or network-bound or database-bound� trend, because performance in those areas is still improving rapidly (gigabit WiFi, anyone?) while traditional CPU performance-enhancing techniques have maxed out. Consider: We�re stopping in the 3GHz range for now. Therefore single-threaded programs are likely not to get much faster any more for now except for benefits from further cache size growth (which is the main good news). Other gains are likely to be incremental and much smaller than we�ve been used to seeing in the past, for example as chip designers find new ways to keep pipelines full and avoid stalls, which are areas where the low-hanging fruit has already been harvested. The demand for new application features is unlikely to abate, and even more so the demand to handle vastly growing quantities of application data is unlikely to stop accelerating. As we continue to demand that programs do more, they will increasingly often find that they run out of CPU to do it unless they can code for concurrency.

There are two ways to deal with this sea change toward concurrency. One is to redesign your applications for concurrency, as above. The other is to be frugal, by writing code that is more efficient and less wasteful. This leads to the third interesting consequence:

3. Efficiency and performance optimization will get more, not less, important. Those languages that already lend themselves to heavy optimization will find new life; those that don�t will need to find ways to compete and become more efficient and optimizable. Expect long-term increased demand for performance-oriented languages and systems.

4. Finally, programming languages and systems will increasingly be forced to deal well with concurrency. The Java language has included support for concurrency since its beginning, although mistakes were made that later had to be corrected over several releases in order to do concurrent programming more correctly and efficiently. The C++ language has long been used to write heavy-duty multithreaded systems well, but it has no standardized support for concurrency at all (the ISO C++ standard doesn�t even mention threads, and does so intentionally), and so typically the concurrency is of necessity accomplished by using nonportable platform-specific concurrency features and libraries. (It�s also often incomplete; for example, static variables must be initialized only once, which typically requires that the compiler wrap them with a lock, but many C++ implementations do not generate the lock.) Finally, there are a few concurrency standards, including pthreads and OpenMP, and some of these support implicit as well as explicit parallelization. Having the compiler look at your single-threaded program and automatically figure out how to parallelize it implicitly is fine and dandy, but those automatic transformation tools are limited and don�t yield nearly the gains of explicit concurrency control that you code yourself. The mainstream state of the art revolves around lock-based programming, which is subtle and hazardous. We desperately need a higher-level programming model for concurrency than languages offer today; I'll have more to say about that soon.

Conclusion

If you haven�t done so already, now is the time to take a hard look at the design of your application, determine what operations are CPU-sensitive now or are likely to become so soon, and identify how those places could benefit from concurrency. Now is also the time for you and your team to grok concurrent programming�s requirements, pitfalls, styles, and idioms.

A few rare classes of applications are naturally parallelizable, but most aren�t. Even when you know exactly where you�re CPU-bound, you may well find it difficult to figure out how to parallelize those operations; all the most reason to start thinking about it now. Implicitly parallelizing compilers can help a little, but don�t expect much; they can�t do nearly as good a job of parallelizing your sequential program as you could do by turning it into an explicitly parallel and threaded version.

Thanks to continued cache growth and probably a few more incremental straight-line control flow optimizations, the free lunch will continue a little while longer; but starting today the buffet will only be serving that one entr�e and that one dessert. The filet mignon of throughput gains is still on the menu, but now it costs extra�extra development effort, extra code complexity, and extra testing effort. The good news is that for many classes of applications the extra effort will be worthwhile, because concurrency will let them fully exploit the continuing exponential gains in processor throughput.

sentences.en: In this article, I�ll describe the changing face of hardware, why it suddenly does matter to software, and how specifically the concurrency revolution matters to you and is going to change the way you will likely be writing software in the future.Arguably, the free lunch has already been over for a year or two, only we�re just now noticing.The Free Performance LunchThere�s an interesting phenomenon that�s known as �Andy giveth, and Bill taketh away.� No matter how fast processors get, software consistently finds new ways to eat up the extra speed.

sentences.zh: （尽管如此，我推测当今实际使用的单线程应用程序实际上可以通过使用双核芯片为大多数用户带来性能提升，不是因为额外的核心实际上做了任何有用的事情，而是因为它正在运行感染许多用户系统的广告软件和间谍软件，否则会降低用户今天拥有的单个 CPU 的速度。

sentences.en: I leave it up to you to decide whether adding a CPU to run your spyware is the best solution to that problem.)If you�re running a single-threaded application, then the application can only make use of one core.
sentences.zh: 我让您自行决定添加 CPU 来运行间谍软件是否是该问题的最佳解决方案。）如果您正在运行单线程应用程序，则该应用程序只能使用一个核心。

sentences.en: There should be some speedup as the operating system and the application can run on separate cores, but typically the OS isn�t going to be maxing out the CPU anyway so one of the cores will be mostly idle.
sentences.zh: 由于操作系统和应用程序可以在单独的内核上运行，因此应该会有一定的加速，但通常操作系统无论如何都不会最大化 CPU，因此其中一个内核将大部分处于空闲状态。

sentences.en: (Again, the spyware can share the OS�s core most of the time.)The key difference, which is the heart of this article, is that the performance gains are going to be accomplished in fundamentally different ways for at least the next couple of processor generations.
sentences.zh: （同样，间谍软件在大多数情况下可以共享操作系统的核心。）关键的区别（也是本文的核心）是，至少在接下来的几代处理器中，性能提升将以根本不同的方式实现。

sentences.en: And most current applications will no longer benefit from the free ride without significant redesign.For the near-term future, meaning for the next few years, the performance gains in new chips will be fueled by three main approaches, only one of which is the same as in the past.
sentences.zh: 如果不进行重大重新设计，大多数当前应用将不再受益于搭便车。在不久的将来，即未来几年，新芯片的性能提升将由三种主要方法推动，其中只有一种与过去相同。

sentences.en: The near-term future performance growth drivers are: hyperthreading multicore cache Hyperthreading is about running two or more threads in parallel inside a single CPU.
sentences.zh: 近期的性能增长驱动因素包括： 超线程 多核缓存 超线程是指在单个 CPU 内并行运行两个或多个线程。

sentences.en: Hyperthreaded CPUs are already available today, and they do allow some instructions to run in parallel.
sentences.zh: 超线程 CPU 现在已经可用，并且它们确实允许一些指令并行运行。

sentences.en: A limiting factor, however, is that although a hyper-threaded CPU has some extra hardware including extra registers, it still has just one cache, one integer math unit, one FPU, and in general just one each of most basic CPU features.
sentences.zh: 然而，一个限制因素是，尽管超线程 CPU 具有一些额外的硬件，包括额外的寄存器，但它仍然只有一个高速缓存、一个整数数学单元、一个 FPU，并且通常只有一个最基本的 CPU 功能。

sentences.en: Hyperthreading is sometimes cited as offering a 5% to 15% performance boost for reasonably well-written multi-threaded applications, or even as much as 40% under ideal conditions for carefully written multi-threaded applications.
sentences.zh: 超线程有时被认为可以为编写得相当好的多线程应用程序提供 5% 到 15% 的性能提升，甚至在理想条件下为精心编写的多线程应用程序提供高达 40% 的性能提升。

sentences.en: That�s good, but it�s hardly double, and it doesn�t help single-threaded applications.Multicore is about running two or more actual CPUs on one chip.
sentences.zh: 这很好，但它几乎不是双核，而且对单线程应用程序没有帮助。多核是指在一个芯片上运行两个或更多实际的 CPU。

sentences.en: Some chips, including Sparc and PowerPC, have multicore versions available already.
sentences.zh: 一些芯片，包括 Sparc 和 PowerPC，已经提供了多核版本。

sentences.en: The initial Intel and AMD designs, both due in 2005, vary in their level of integration but are functionally similar.
sentences.zh: Intel 和 AMD 的最初设计均于 2005 年推出，它们的集成程度有所不同，但功能相似。

sentences.en: AMD�s seems to have some initial performance design advantages, such as better integration of support functions on the same die, whereas Intel�s initial entry basically just glues together two Xeons on a single die.
sentences.zh: AMD 似乎具有一些初始性能设计优势，例如在同一芯片上更好地集成支持功能，而英特尔最初的产品基本上只是将两个 Xeon 粘合在一个芯片上。

sentences.en: The performance gains should initially be about the same as having a true dual-CPU system (only the system will be cheaper because the motherboard doesn�t have to have two sockets and associated �glue� chippery), which means something less than double the speed even in the ideal case, and just like today it will boost reasonably well-written multi-threaded applications.
sentences.zh: 性能增益最初应该与真正的双 CPU 系统大致相同（只是该系统会更便宜，因为主板不必有两个插槽和相关的“粘合”芯片），这意味着即使在理想情况下速度也不会增加一倍，就像今天一样，它将提高编写得相当好的多线程应用程序。

sentences.en: Not single-threaded ones.Finally, on-die cache sizes can be expected to continue to grow, at least in the near term.
sentences.zh: 不是单线程的。最后，片上缓存大小预计将继续增长，至少在短期内如此。

sentences.en: Of these three areas, only this one will broadly benefit most existing applications.
sentences.zh: 在这三个领域中，只有这一领域将使大多数现有应用程序广泛受益。

sentences.en: The continuing growth in on-die cache sizes is an incredibly important and highly applicable benefit for many applications, simply because space is speed.
sentences.zh: 对于许多应用程序来说，片上缓存大小的持续增长是一个极其重要且高度适用的优势，因为空间就是速度。

sentences.en: Accessing main memory is expensive, and you really don�t want to touch RAM if you can help it.
sentences.zh: 访问主内存的成本很高，如果可以的话，你真的不想碰 RAM。

sentences.en: On today�s systems, a cache miss that goes out to main memory often costs 10 to 50 times as much getting the information from the cache; this, incidentally, continues to surprise people because we all think of memory as fast, and it is fast compared to disks and networks, but not compared to on-board cache which runs at faster speeds.
sentences.zh: 在当今的系统中，发送到主内存的高速缓存未命中的成本通常是从高速缓存获取信息的成本的 10 到 50 倍；顺便说一句，这仍然让人们感到惊讶，因为我们都认为内存速度很快，而且与磁盘和网络相比，它的速度很快，但与运行速度更快的板载缓存相比却不然。

sentences.en: If an application�s working set fits into cache, we�re golden, and if it doesn�t, we�re not.
sentences.zh: 如果应用程序的工作集适合缓存，我们就是黄金，如果不适合，我们就不是。

sentences.en: That is why increased cache sizes will save some existing applications and breathe life into them for a few more years without requiring significant redesign: As existing applications manipulate more and more data, and as they are incrementally updated to include more code for new features, performance-sensitive operations need to continue to fit into cache.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么增加缓存大小将节省一些现有应用程序，并让它们多活几年，而无需进行重大重新设计：随着现有应用程序操作越来越多的数据，并且随着它们逐步更新以包含更多新功能代码，性能敏感的操作需要继续适应缓存。

sentences.en: As the Depression-era old-timers will be quick to remind you, �Cache is king.�(Aside: Here�s an anecdote to demonstrate �space is speed� that recently hit my compiler team.
sentences.zh: 正如大萧条时代的老前辈们会很快提醒您的那样，“缓存为王”。（旁白：这是一个最近影响我的编译器团队的轶事，展示了“空间就是速度”。

sentences.en: The compiler uses the same source base for the 32-bit and 64-bit compilers; the code is just compiled as either a 32-bit process or a 64-bit one.
sentences.zh: 32 位和 64 位编译器使用相同的源代码库；该代码只是编译为 32 位进程或 64 位进程。

sentences.en: The 64-bit compiler gained a great deal of baseline performance by running on a 64-bit CPU, principally because the 64-bit CPU had many more registers to work with and had other code performance features.
sentences.zh: 64 位编译器通过在 64 位 CPU 上运行获得了大量的基准性能，主要是因为 64 位 CPU 有更多的寄存器可供使用，并且具有其他代码性能特性。

sentences.en: All well and good.
sentences.zh: 一切都很好。

sentences.en: But what about data?
sentences.zh: 但数据呢？

sentences.en: Going to 64 bits didn�t change the size of most of the data in memory, except that of course pointers in particular were now twice the size they were before.
sentences.zh: 变为 64 位并没有改变内存中大部分数据的大小，当然，尤其是指针的大小现在是以前的两倍。

sentences.en: As it happens, our compiler uses pointers much more heavily in its internal data structures than most other kinds of applications ever would.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们的编译器在其内部数据结构中使用指针的次数比大多数其他类型的应用程序要多得多。

sentences.en: Because pointers were now 8 bytes instead of 4 bytes, a pure data size increase, we saw a significant increase in the 64-bit compiler�s working set.
sentences.zh: 由于指针现在由 4 字节变为 8 字节，纯粹的数据大小增加，因此我们看到 64 位编译器的工作集显着增加。

sentences.en: That bigger working set caused a performance penalty that almost exactly offset the code execution performance increase we�d gained from going to the faster processor with more registers.
sentences.zh: 更大的工作集导致了性能损失，几乎完全抵消了我们通过使用具有更多寄存器的更快处理器而获得的代码执行性能提升。

sentences.en: As of this writing, the 64-bit compiler runs at the same speed as the 32-bit compiler, even though the source base is the same for both and the 64-bit processor offers better raw processing throughput.
sentences.zh: 截至撰写本文时，64 位编译器的运行速度与 32 位编译器相同，尽管两者的源代码库相同，并且 64 位处理器提供了更好的原始处理吞吐量。

sentences.en: Space is speed.)But cache is it.
sentences.zh: 空间就是速度。）但是缓存就是它。

sentences.en: Hyperthreading and multicore CPUs will have nearly no impact on most current applications.So what does this change in the hardware mean for the way we write software?
sentences.zh: 超线程和多核 CPU 对当前大多数应用程序几乎没有影响。那么硬件的这种变化对我们编写软件的方式意味着什么呢？

sentences.en: By now you�ve probably noticed the basic answer, so let�s consider it and its consequences.What This Means For Software: The Next RevolutionIn the 1990s, we learned to grok objects.
sentences.zh: 现在您可能已经注意到了基本答案，所以让我们考虑一下它及其后果。这对软件意味着什么：下一次革命在 20 世纪 90 年代，我们学会了理解对象。

sentences.en: The revolution in mainstream software development from structured programming to object-oriented programming was the greatest such change in the past 20 years, and arguably in the past 30 years.
sentences.zh: 主流软件开发从结构化编程到面向对象编程的革命是过去 20 年（甚至可以说是过去 30 年）最大的变革。

sentences.en: There have been other changes, including the most recent (and genuinely interesting) naissance of web services, but nothing that most of us have seen during our careers has been as fundamental and as far-reaching a change in the way we write software as the object revolution.Until now.Starting today, the performance lunch isn�t free any more.
sentences.zh: 还有其他变化，包括最近（并且真正有趣）的 Web 服务的诞生，但我们大多数人在我们的职业生涯中所看到的没有像对象革命那样对我们编写软件的方式产生如此根本和深远的变化。直到现在。从今天开始，性能午餐不再是免费的。

sentences.en: Sure, there will continue to be generally applicable performance gains that everyone can pick up, thanks mainly to cache size improvements.
sentences.zh: 当然，每个人都可以继续获得普遍适用的性能提升，这主要归功于缓存大小的改进。

sentences.en: But if you want your application to benefit from the continued exponential throughput advances in new processors, it will need to be a well-written concurrent (usually multithreaded) application.
sentences.zh: 但是，如果您希望您的应用程序受益于新处理器中持续呈指数级增长的吞吐量增长，则它需要是一个编写良好的并发（通常是多线程）应用程序。

sentences.en: And that�s easier said than done, because not all problems are inherently parallelizable and because concurrent programming is hard.I can hear the howls of protest: �Concurrency?
sentences.zh: 这说起来容易做起来难，因为并非所有问题本质上都是可并行的，而且并发编程很难。我可以听到抗议的呼声：“并发？”

sentences.en: That�s not news!
sentences.zh: 这不是新闻！

sentences.en: People are already writing concurrent applications.� That�s true.
sentences.zh: 人们已经在编写并发应用程序了。确实如此。

sentences.en: Of a small fraction of developers.Remember that people have been doing object-oriented programming since at least the days of Simula in the late 1960s.
sentences.zh: 只占一小部分开发人员。请记住，至少从 20 世纪 60 年代末的 Simula 时代起，人们就一直在进行面向对象编程。

sentences.en: But OO didn�t become a revolution, and dominant in the mainstream, until the 1990s.
sentences.zh: 但直到 20 世纪 90 年代，面向对象才成为一场革命，并在主流中占据主导地位。

sentences.en: Why then?
sentences.zh: 那为什么呢？

sentences.en: The reason the revolution happened was primarily that our industry was driven by requirements to write larger and larger systems that solved larger and larger problems and exploited the greater and greater CPU and storage resources that were becoming available.
sentences.zh: 这场革命发生的主要原因是，我们的行业受到编写越来越大的系统的需求的驱动，这些系统解决了越来越大的问题，并利用了越来越多的可用 CPU 和存储资源。

sentences.en: OOP�s strengths in abstraction and dependency management made it a necessity for achieving large-scale software development that is economical, reliable, and repeatable.Concurrency is the next major revolution in how we write softwareSimilarly, we�ve been doing concurrent programming since those same dark ages, writing coroutines and monitors and similar jazzy stuff.
sentences.zh: OOP 在抽象和依赖管理方面的优势使其成为实现经济、可靠和可重复的大规模软件开发的必要条件。并发性是我们编写软件方式的下一场重大革命同样，我们从那些黑暗时代开始就一直在进行并发编程，编写协程和监视器以及类似的爵士乐东西。

sentences.en: And for the past decade or so we�ve witnessed incrementally more and more programmers writing concurrent (multi-threaded, multi-process) systems.
sentences.zh: 在过去十年左右的时间里，我们目睹了越来越多的程序员编写并发（多线程、多进程）系统。

sentences.en: But an actual revolution marked by a major turning point toward concurrency has been slow to materialize.
sentences.zh: 但以并发性重大转折为标志的真正革命却迟迟没有实现。

sentences.en: Today the vast majority of applications are single-threaded, and for good reasons that I�ll summarize in the next section.By the way, on the matter of hype: People have always been quick to announce �the next software development revolution,� usually about their own brand-new technology.
sentences.zh: 今天，绝大多数应用程序都是单线程的，这是有充分理由的，我将在下一节中总结。顺便说一句，关于炒作：人们总是很快宣布“下一次软件开发革命”，通常是关于他们自己的全新技术。

sentences.en: Don�t believe it.
sentences.zh: 别相信。

sentences.en: New technologies are often genuinely interesting and sometimes beneficial, but the biggest revolutions in the way we write software generally come from technologies that have already been around for some years and have already experienced gradual growth before they transition to explosive growth.
sentences.zh: 新技术通常确实很有趣，有时甚至是有益的，但我们编写软件方式的最大革命通常来自已经存在多年的技术，并且在过渡到爆炸性增长之前已经经历了逐渐增长。

sentences.en: This is necessary: You can only base a software development revolution on a technology that�s mature enough to build on (including having solid vendor and tool support), and it generally takes any new software technology at least seven years before it�s solid enough to be broadly usable without performance cliffs and other gotchas.
sentences.zh: 这是必要的：您只能将软件开发革命建立在足够成熟的技术之上（包括拥有可靠的供应商和工具支持），并且任何新的软件技术通常至少需要七年才能足够可靠以广泛使用，而不会出现性能悬崖和其他问题。

sentences.en: As a result, true software development revolutions like OO happen around technologies that have already been undergoing refinement for years, often decades.
sentences.zh: 因此，像面向对象这样的真正的软件开发革命发生在已经经过多年（通常是几十年）改进的技术周围。

sentences.en: Even in Hollywood, most genuine �overnight successes� have really been performing for many years before their big break.Concurrency is the next major revolution in how we write software.
sentences.zh: 即使在好莱坞，大多数真正的“一夜成功”在取得重大突破之前实际上已经持续了很多年。并发性是我们编写软件方式的下一次重大革命。

sentences.en: Different experts still have different opinions on whether it will be bigger than OO, but that kind of conversation is best left to pundits.
sentences.zh: 对于它是否会比 OO 更大，不同的专家仍然有不同的看法，但这种讨论最好留给专家们。

sentences.en: For technologists, the interesting thing is that concurrency is of the same order as OO both in the (expected) scale of the revolution and in the complexity and learning curve of the technology.Benefits and Costs of ConcurrencyThere are two major reasons for which concurrency, especially multithreading, is already used in mainstream software.
sentences.zh: 对于技术人员来说，有趣的是，无论是在（预期的）革命规模还是技术的复杂性和学习曲线上，并发性都与 OO 处于同一数量级。 并发性的好处和成本 并发性（尤其是多线程）已经在主流软件中使用有两个主要原因。

sentences.en: The first is to logically separate naturally independent control flows; for example, in a database replication server I designed it was natural to put each replication session on its own thread, because each session worked completely independently of any others that might be active (as long as they weren�t working on the same database row).
sentences.zh: 一是逻辑上分离自然独立的控制流；例如，在我设计的数据库复制服务器中，很自然地将每个复制会话放在自己的线程上，因为每个会话完全独立于任何其他可能处于活动状态的会话（只要它们不在同一数据库行上工作）。

sentences.en: The second and less common reason to write concurrent code in the past has been for performance, either to scalably take advantage of multiple physical CPUs or to easily take advantage of latency in other parts of the application; in my database replication server, this factor applied as well and the separate threads were able to scale well on multiple CPUs as our server handled more and more concurrent replication sessions with many other servers.There are, however, real costs to concurrency.
sentences.zh: 过去编写并发代码的第二个也是不太常见的原因是为了性能，要么是为了可扩展地利用多个物理 CPU，要么是为了轻松地利用应用程序其他部分的延迟；在我的数据库复制服务器中，这个因素也适用，并且随着我们的服务器处理与许多其他服务器越来越多的并发复制会话，单独的线程能够在多个 CPU 上很好地扩展。然而，并发性是有实际成本的。

sentences.en: Some of the obvious costs are actually relatively unimportant.
sentences.zh: 一些明显的成本实际上相对不重要。

sentences.en: For example, yes, locks can be expensive to acquire, but when used judiciously and properly you gain much more from the concurrent execution than you lose on the synchronization, if you can find a sensible way to parallelize the operation and minimize or eliminate shared state.Perhaps the second-greatest cost of concurrency is that not all applications are amenable to parallelization.
sentences.zh: 例如，是的，获取锁的成本可能很高，但如果明智且正确地使用，如果您能找到一种合理的方法来并行化操作并最小化或消除共享状态，那么您从并发执行中获得的收益远多于在同步中损失的收益。也许并发的第二大成本是并非所有应用程序都适合并行化。

sentences.en: I�ll say more about this later on.Probably the greatest cost of concurrency is that concurrency really is hard: The programming model, meaning the model in the programmer�s head that he needs to reason reliably about his program, is much harder than it is for sequential control flow.Everybody who learns concurrency thinks they understand it, ends up finding mysterious races they thought weren�t possible, and discovers that they didn�t actually understand it yet after all.
sentences.zh: 我稍后会详细讨论这一点。并发性的最大成本可能是并发性确实很困难：编程模型，即程序员头脑中需要可靠地推理其程序的模型，比顺序控制流要困难得多。每个学习并发性的人都认为自己理解它，最终发现他们认为不可能的神秘竞赛，并发现他们实际上还没有理解它。

sentences.en: As the developer learns to reason about concurrency, they find that usually those races can be caught by reasonable in-house testing, and they reach a new plateau of knowledge and comfort.
sentences.zh: 当开发人员学会推理并发性时，他们发现通常可以通过合理的内部测试来捕获这些竞争，并且他们达到了知识和舒适度的新水平。

sentences.en: What usually doesn�t get caught in testing, however, except in shops that understand why and how to do real stress testing, is those latent concurrency bugs that surface only on true multiprocessor systems, where the threads aren�t just being switched around on a single processor but where they really do execute truly simultaneously and thus expose new classes of errors.
sentences.zh: 然而，除了了解为什么以及如何进行真正的压力测试的商店之外，测试中通常不会发现的是那些仅在真正的多处理器系统上出现的潜在并发错误，其中线程不仅在单个处理器上切换，而且它们确实真正同时执行，从而暴露了新的错误类别。

sentences.en: This is the next jolt for people who thought that surely now they know how to write concurrent code: I�ve come across many teams whose application worked fine even under heavy and extended stress testing, and ran perfectly at many customer sites, until the day that a customer actually had a real multiprocessor machine and then deeply mysterious races and corruptions started to manifest intermittently.
sentences.zh: 对于那些自认为现在肯定知道如何编写并发代码的人来说，这是下一个震动：我遇到过许多团队，他们的应用程序即使在繁重和扩展的压力测试下也能正常工作，并且在许多客户站点上完美运行，直到有一天，客户实际上拥有了真正的多处理器计算机，然后深深神秘的竞争和损坏开始间歇性地显现出来。

sentences.en: In the context of today�s CPU landscape, then, redesigning your application to run multithreaded on a multicore machine is a little like learning to swim by jumping into the deep end�going straight to the least forgiving, truly parallel environment that is most likely to expose the things you got wrong.

sentences.en: Even when you have a team that can reliably write safe concurrent code, there are other pitfalls; for example, concurrent code that is completely safe but isn�t any faster than it was on a single-core machine, typically because the threads aren�t independent enough and share a dependency on a single resource which re-serializes the program�s execution.
sentences.zh: 即使您拥有一个可以可靠地编写安全并发代码的团队，也存在其他陷阱；例如，并发代码是完全安全的，但并不比单核机器上的速度快，通常是因为线程不够独立，并且共享对重新序列化程序执行的单个资源的依赖。

sentences.en: But the concurrent programming model is learnable, particularly if we stick to message- and lock-based programming, and once grokked it isn�t that much harder than OO and hopefully can become just as natural.

sentences.en: Just be ready and allow for the investment in training and time, for you and for your team.(I deliberately limit the above to message- and lock-based concurrent programming models.

sentences.en: There is also lock-free programming, supported most directly at the language level in Java 5 and in at least one popular C++ compiler.
sentences.zh: 还有无锁编程，在 Java 5 的语言级别和至少一种流行的 C++ 编译器中得到最直接的支持。

sentences.en: But concurrent lock-free programming is known to be very much harder for programmers to understand and reason about than even concurrent lock-based programming.
sentences.zh: 但众所周知，并发无锁编程比基于并发锁的编程更难理解和推理。

sentences.en: Most of the time, only systems and library writers should have to understand lock-free programming, although virtually everybody should be able to take advantage of the lock-free systems and libraries those people produce.
sentences.zh: 大多数时候，只有系统和库编写者应该了解无锁编程，尽管实际上每个人都应该能够利用这些人制作的无锁系统和库。

sentences.en: Frankly, even lock-based programming is hazardous.)What It Means For UsOkay, back to what it means for us.1.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，即使基于锁的编程也是危险的。）这对我们意味着什么好吧，回到它对我们意味着什么。1。

sentences.en: The clear primary consequence we�ve already covered is that applications will increasingly need to be concurrent if they want to fully exploit CPU throughput gains that have now started becoming available and will continue to materialize over the next several years.
sentences.zh: 我们已经讨论过的一个明显的主要结果是，如果应用程序想要充分利用 CPU 吞吐量的提升，那么它们将越来越需要并发，而这些提升现在已经开始可用，并将在未来几年内继续实现。

sentences.en: For example, Intel is talking about someday producing 100-core chips; a single-threaded application can exploit at most 1/100 of such a chip�s potential throughput. �Oh, performance doesn�t matter so much, computers just keep getting faster� has always been a na�ve statement to be viewed with suspicion, and for the near future it will almost always be simply wrong.Applications will increasingly need to be concurrent if they want to fully exploit continuing exponential CPU throughput gainsEfficiency and performance optimization will get more, not less, importantNow, not all applications (or, more precisely, important operations of an application) are amenable to parallelization.
sentences.zh: 例如，英特尔正在谈论有一天生产 100 核芯片；单线程应用程序最多可以利用此类芯片潜在吞吐量的 1/100。 “哦，性能并不那么重要，计算机只是变得越来越快”一直是一个令人怀疑的天真的说法，在不久的将来，它几乎总是完全错误的。如果应用程序想要充分利用持续呈指数级增长的 CPU 吞吐量收益，那么它们将越来越需要并发。效率和性能优化将变得更加重要，而不是更少。现在，并非所有应用程序（或者更准确地说，应用程序的重要操作）都适合并行化。

sentences.en: True, some problems, such as compilation, are almost ideally parallelizable.
sentences.zh: 确实，有些问题（例如编译）几乎可以理想地并行化。

sentences.en: But others aren�t; the usual counterexample here is that just because it takes one woman nine months to produce a baby doesn�t imply that nine women could produce one baby in one month.
sentences.zh: 但其他人则不然；这里通常的反例是，仅仅因为一名妇女需要九个月才能生下一个孩子，并不意味着九名妇女可以在一个月内生下一个孩子。

sentences.en: You�ve probably come across that analogy before.
sentences.zh: 您以前可能遇到过这个类比。

sentences.en: But did you notice the problem with leaving the analogy at that?
sentences.zh: 但你有没有注意到这样的类比会带来问题吗？

sentences.en: Here�s the trick question to ask the next person who uses it on you: Can you conclude from this that the Human Baby Problem is inherently not amenable to parallelization?
sentences.zh: 这是一个棘手的问题，可以问下一个在你身上使用它的人：你能从中得出结论，人类婴儿问题本质上不适合并行化吗？

sentences.en: Usually people relating this analogy err in quickly concluding that it demonstrates an inherently nonparallel problem, but that�s actually not necessarily correct at all.
sentences.zh: 通常，人们在进行这个类比时会错误地很快得出结论，认为它展示了一个本质上不平行的问题，但这实际上根本不一定正确。

sentences.en: It is indeed an inherently nonparallel problem if the goal is to produce one child.
sentences.zh: 如果目标是生一个孩子，这确实是一个本质上不可平行的问题。

sentences.en: It is actually an ideally parallelizable problem if the goal is to produce many children!
sentences.zh: 如果目标是产生许多孩子，这实际上是一个理想的可并行问题！

sentences.en: Knowing the real goals can make all the difference.
sentences.zh: 了解真正的目标可以让一切变得不同。

sentences.en: This basic goal-oriented principle is something to keep in mind when considering whether and how to parallelize your software.2.
sentences.zh: 在考虑是否以及如何并行化您的软件时，请牢记这一基本的面向目标的原则。2．

sentences.en: Perhaps a less obvious consequence is that applications are likely to become increasingly CPU-bound.
sentences.zh: 也许一个不太明显的后果是应用程序可能会变得越来越受 CPU 限制。

sentences.en: Of course, not every application operation will be CPU-bound, and even those that will be affected won�t become CPU-bound overnight if they aren�t already, but we seem to have reached the end of the �applications are increasingly I/O-bound or network-bound or database-bound� trend, because performance in those areas is still improving rapidly (gigabit WiFi, anyone?)
sentences.zh: 当然，并不是每个应用程序操作都会受 CPU 限制，即使那些受影响的应用程序操作也不会一夜之间变得受 CPU 限制（如果还没有的话），但我们似乎已经到了“应用程序越来越受 I/O 限制、网络限制或数据库限制”趋势的终结，因为这些领域的性能仍在快速提高（千兆位 WiFi，有人吗？）

sentences.en: while traditional CPU performance-enhancing techniques have maxed out.
sentences.zh: 而传统的CPU性能增强技术已经达到极限。

sentences.en: Consider: We�re stopping in the 3GHz range for now.
sentences.zh: 考虑一下：我们现在停留在 3GHz 范围内。

sentences.en: Therefore single-threaded programs are likely not to get much faster any more for now except for benefits from further cache size growth (which is the main good news).
sentences.zh: 因此，除了缓存大小进一步增长带来的好处（这是主要的好消息）之外，单线程程序目前可能不会再变得更快。

sentences.en: Other gains are likely to be incremental and much smaller than we�ve been used to seeing in the past, for example as chip designers find new ways to keep pipelines full and avoid stalls, which are areas where the low-hanging fruit has already been harvested.
sentences.zh: 其他收益可能是渐进式的，而且比我们过去所看到的要小得多，例如，芯片设计人员找到了保持管道满载并避免停滞的新方法，而这些领域已经收获了唾手可得的成果。

sentences.en: The demand for new application features is unlikely to abate, and even more so the demand to handle vastly growing quantities of application data is unlikely to stop accelerating.
sentences.zh: 对新应用程序功能的需求不太可能减弱，更重要的是，处理数量大幅增长的应用程序数据的需求不太可能停止加速。

sentences.en: As we continue to demand that programs do more, they will increasingly often find that they run out of CPU to do it unless they can code for concurrency.There are two ways to deal with this sea change toward concurrency.
sentences.zh: 当我们不断要求程序做更多事情时，他们会越来越频繁地发现，除非他们能够编写并发性代码，否则他们会耗尽 CPU 来完成这些工作。有两种方法可以应对并发性的巨大变化。

sentences.en: One is to redesign your applications for concurrency, as above.
sentences.zh: 一是重新设计应用程序以实现并发性，如上所述。

sentences.en: The other is to be frugal, by writing code that is more efficient and less wasteful.
sentences.zh: 另一个是节俭，编写更高效、更少浪费的代码。

sentences.en: This leads to the third interesting consequence:3.
sentences.zh: 这导致了第三个有趣的结果：3。

sentences.en: Efficiency and performance optimization will get more, not less, important.
sentences.zh: 效率和性能优化将变得更加重要，而不是不那么重要。

sentences.en: Those languages that already lend themselves to heavy optimization will find new life; those that don�t will need to find ways to compete and become more efficient and optimizable.
sentences.zh: 那些已经适合进行大量优化的语言将获得新的生命；那些不这样做的人将需要找到竞争的方法并变得更加高效和优化。

sentences.en: Expect long-term increased demand for performance-oriented languages and systems.4.
sentences.zh: 预计对面向性能的语言和系统的需求将长期增长。4．

sentences.en: Finally, programming languages and systems will increasingly be forced to deal well with concurrency.
sentences.zh: 最后，编程语言和系统将越来越被迫妥善处理并发性。

sentences.en: The Java language has included support for concurrency since its beginning, although mistakes were made that later had to be corrected over several releases in order to do concurrent programming more correctly and efficiently.
sentences.zh: Java 语言从一开始就包含了对并发的支持，尽管犯了一些错误，后来必须在多个版本中进行纠正，以便更正确、更高效地进行并发编程。

sentences.en: The C++ language has long been used to write heavy-duty multithreaded systems well, but it has no standardized support for concurrency at all (the ISO C++ standard doesn�t even mention threads, and does so intentionally), and so typically the concurrency is of necessity accomplished by using nonportable platform-specific concurrency features and libraries.
sentences.zh: C++ 语言长期以来一直被用来编写重型多线程系统，但它根本没有对并发的标准化支持（ISO C++ 标准甚至没有提到线程，并且是故意这样做的），因此通常必须通过使用不可移植的特定于平台的并发功能和库来实现并发。

sentences.en: (It�s also often incomplete; for example, static variables must be initialized only once, which typically requires that the compiler wrap them with a lock, but many C++ implementations do not generate the lock.)
sentences.zh: （它通常也是不完整的；例如，静态变量只能初始化一次，这通常要求编译器用锁包装它们，但许多 C++ 实现不会生成锁。）

sentences.en: Finally, there are a few concurrency standards, including pthreads and OpenMP, and some of these support implicit as well as explicit parallelization.
sentences.zh: 最后，还有一些并发标准，包括 pthreads 和 OpenMP，其中一些标准支持隐式和显式并行化。

sentences.en: Having the compiler look at your single-threaded program and automatically figure out how to parallelize it implicitly is fine and dandy, but those automatic transformation tools are limited and don�t yield nearly the gains of explicit concurrency control that you code yourself.
sentences.zh: 让编译器查看您的单线程程序并自动找出如何隐式并行化它是很好的，但这些自动转换工具是有限的，并且不会产生您自己编写的显式并发控制的收益。

sentences.en: The mainstream state of the art revolves around lock-based programming, which is subtle and hazardous.
sentences.zh: 主流的技术水平围绕基于锁的编程，这是微妙且危险的。

sentences.en: We desperately need a higher-level programming model for concurrency than languages offer today; I'll have more to say about that soon.ConclusionIf you haven�t done so already, now is the time to take a hard look at the design of your application, determine what operations are CPU-sensitive now or are likely to become so soon, and identify how those places could benefit from concurrency.
sentences.zh: 我们迫切需要比当今语言提供的更高级别的并发编程模型；我很快就会对此有更多内容要说。结论如果您还没有这样做，那么现在是时候仔细检查应用程序的设计，确定哪些操作现在或可能很快变得对 CPU 敏感，并确定这些地方如何从并发中受益。

sentences.en: Now is also the time for you and your team to grok concurrent programming�s requirements, pitfalls, styles, and idioms.A few rare classes of applications are naturally parallelizable, but most aren�t.
sentences.zh: 现在也是您和您的团队了解并发编程的要求、陷阱、风格和习惯用法的时候了。少数罕见的应用程序类别自然是可并行的，但大多数都不是。

sentences.en: Even when you know exactly where you�re CPU-bound, you may well find it difficult to figure out how to parallelize those operations; all the most reason to start thinking about it now.
sentences.zh: 即使您确切地知道哪里受 CPU 限制，您也可能会发现很难弄清楚如何并行化这些操作；现在就开始考虑这个问题是最有理由的。

sentences.en: Implicitly parallelizing compilers can help a little, but don�t expect much; they can�t do nearly as good a job of parallelizing your sequential program as you could do by turning it into an explicitly parallel and threaded version.Thanks to continued cache growth and probably a few more incremental straight-line control flow optimizations, the free lunch will continue a little while longer; but starting today the buffet will only be serving that one entr�e and that one dessert.
sentences.zh: 隐式并行编译器可以提供一点帮助，但不要期望太多；它们无法像通过将顺序程序转变为显式并行和线程版本那样出色地并行化顺序程序。由于缓存的持续增长以及可能更多的增量直线控制流优化，免费午餐将持续一段时间；但从今天开始，自助餐将只提供一份主菜和一份甜点。

sentences.en: The filet mignon of throughput gains is still on the menu, but now it costs extra�extra development effort, extra code complexity, and extra testing effort.
sentences.zh: 吞吐量增益的菲力牛排仍然在菜单上，但现在它需要额外的开发工作、额外的代码复杂性和额外的测试工作。

sentences.en: The good news is that for many classes of applications the extra effort will be worthwhile, because concurrency will let them fully exploit the continuing exponential gains in processor throughput.
sentences.zh: 好消息是，对于许多类别的应用程序来说，额外的努力是值得的，因为并发性将使它们充分利用处理器吞吐量的持续指数增长。

blocks.html_en: The major processor manufacturers and architectures, from Intel and AMD to Sparc and PowerPC, have run out of room with most of their traditional approaches to boosting CPU performance. Instead of driving clock speeds and straight-line instruction throughput ever higher, they are instead turning en masse to hyperthreading and multicore architectures. Both of these features are already available on chips today; in particular, multicore is available on current PowerPC and Sparc IV processors, and is coming in 2005 from Intel and AMD. Indeed, the big theme of the 2004 In-Stat/MDR Fall Processor Forum was multicore devices, as many companies showed new or updated multicore processors. blocks.html_en: 4. Finally, programming languages and systems will increasingly be forced to deal well with concurrency. The Java language has included support for concurrency since its beginning, although mistakes were made that later had to be corrected over several releases in order to do concurrent programming more correctly and efficiently. The C++ language has long been used to write heavy-duty multithreaded systems well, but it has no standardized support for concurrency at all (the ISO C++ standard doesn�t even mention threads, and does so intentionally), and so typically the concurrency is of necessity accomplished by using nonportable platform-specific concurrency features and libraries. (It�s also often incomplete; for example, static variables must be initialized only once, which typically requires that the compiler wrap them with a lock, but many C++ implementations do not generate the lock.) Finally, there are a few concurrency standards, including pthreads and OpenMP, and some of these support implicit as well as explicit parallelization. Having the compiler look at your single-threaded program and automatically figure out how to parallelize it implicitly is fine and dandy, but those automatic transformation tools are limited and don�t yield nearly the gains of explicit concurrency control that you code yourself. The mainstream state of the art revolves around lock-based programming, which is subtle and hazardous. We desperately need a higher-level programming model for concurrency than languages offer today; I'll have more to say about that soon.

这是必要的：您只能将软件开发革命建立在足够成熟的技术之上（包括拥有可靠的供应商和工具支持），并且任何新的软件技术通常至少需要七年才能足够可靠以广泛使用，而不会出现性能悬崖和其他问题。 因此，像面向对象这样的真正的软件开发革命发生在已经经过多年（通常是几十年）改进的技术周围。 即使在好莱坞，大多数真正的“一夜成功”在取得重大突破之前实际上已经持续了很多年。并发性是我们编写软件方式的下一次重大革命。 对于它是否会比 OO 更大，不同的专家仍然有不同的看法，但这种讨论最好留给专家们。 对于技术人员来说，有趣的是，无论是在（预期的）革命规模还是技术的复杂性和学习曲线上，并发性都与 OO 处于同一数量级。 并发性的好处和成本 并发性（尤其是多线程）已经在主流软件中使用有两个主要原因。 一是逻辑上分离自然独立的控制流；例如，在我设计的数据库复制服务器中，很自然地将每个复制会话放在自己的线程上，因为每个会话完全独立于任何其他可能处于活动状态的会话（只要它们不在同一数据库行上工作）。 过去编写并发代码的第二个也是不太常见的原因是为了性能，要么是为了可扩展地利用多个物理 我稍后会详细讨论这一点。并发性的最大成本可能是并发性确实很困难：编程模型，即程序员头脑中需要可靠地推理其程序的模型，比顺序控制流要困难得多。每个学习并发性的人都认为自己理解它，最终发现他们认为不可能的神秘竞赛，并发现他们实际上还没有理解它。 当开发人员学会推理并发性时，他们发现通常可以通过合理的内部测试来捕获这些竞争，并且他们达到了知识和舒适度的新水平。 然而，除了了解为什么以及如何进行真正的压力测试的商店之外，测试中通常不会发现的是那些仅在真正的多处理器系统上出现的潜在并发错误，其中线程不仅在单个处理器上切换，而且它们确实真正同时执行，从而暴露了新的错误类别。 对于那些自认为现在肯定知道如何编写并发代码的人来说，这是下一个震动：我遇到过许多团队，他们的应用程序即使在繁重和扩展的压力测试下也能正常工作，并且在许多客户站点上完美运行，直到有一天，客户实际上拥有了真正的多处理器计算机，然后深深神秘的竞争和损坏开始间歇性地显现出来。 那么，在当今 CPU 我们已经讨论过的一个明显的主要结果是，如果应用程序想要充分利用 CPU 吞吐量的提升，那么它们将越来越需要并发，而这些提升现在已经开始可用，并将在未来几年内继续实现。 例如，英特尔正在谈论有一天生产 100 核芯片；单线程应用程序最多可以利用此类芯片潜在吞吐量的 1/100。 “哦，性能并不那么重要，计算机只是变得越来越快”一直是一个令人怀疑的天真的说法，在不久的将来，它几乎总是完全错误的。如果应用程序想要充分利用持续呈指数级增长的 CPU 吞吐量收益，那么它们将越来越需要并发。效率和性能优化将变得更加重要，而不是更少。现在，并非所有应用程序（或者更准确地说，应用程序的重要操作）都适合并行化。 确实，有些问题（例如编译）几乎可以理想地并行化。 但其他人则不然；这里通常的反例是，仅仅因为一名妇女需要九个月才能生下一个孩子，并不意味着九名妇女可以在一个月内生下一个孩子。 您以前可能遇到过这个类比。 但你有没有注意到这样的类比会带来问题吗？ 这是一个棘手的问题，可以问下一个在你身上使用它的人：你能从中得出结论，人类婴儿问题本质上不适合并行化吗？ 通常，人们在进行这个类比时会错误地很快得出结论，认为它展示了一个本质上不平行的问题，但这实际上根本不一定正确。 如果目标是生一个孩子，这确实是一个本质上不可平行的问题。 如果目标是产生许多孩子，这实际上是一个理想的可并行问题！ 了解真正的目标可以让一切变得不同。 在考虑是否以及如何并行化您的软件时，请牢记这一基本的面向目标的原则。2． 也许一个不太明显的后果是应用程序可能会变得越来越受 CPU 限制。 当然，并不是每个应用程序操作都会受 CPU 限制，即使那些受影响的应用程序操作也不会一夜之间变得受 CPU 限制（如果还没有的话），但我们似乎已经到了“应用程序越来越受 I/O 限制、网络限制或数据库限制”趋势的终结，因为这些领域的性能仍在快速提高（千兆位 WiFi，有人吗？） 而传统的CPU性能增强技术已经达到极限。 考虑一下：我们现在停留在 3GHz 范围内。 因此，除了缓存大小进一步增长带来的好处（这是主要的好消息）之外，单线程程序目前可能不会再变得更快。 其他收益可能是渐进式的，而且比我们过去所看到的要小得多，例如，芯片设计人员找到了保持管道满载并避免停滞的新方法，而这些领域已经收获了唾手可得的成果。 对新应用程序功能的需求不太可能减弱，更重要的是，处理数量大幅增长的应用程序数据的需求不太可能停止加速。 当我们不断要求程序做更多事情时，他们会越来越频繁地发现，除非他们能够编写并发性代码，否则他们会耗尽 CPU 来完成这些工作。有两种方法可以应对并发性的巨大变化。 一是重新设计应用程序以实现并发性，如上所述。 另一个是节俭，编写更高效、更少浪费的代码。 这导致了第三个有趣的结果：3。 效率和性能优化将变得更加重要，而不是不那么重要。 那些已经适合进行大量优化的语言将获得新的生命；那些不这样做的人将需要找到竞争的方法并变得更加高效和优化。 预计对面向性能的语言和系统的需求将长期增长。4． 最后，编程语言和系统将越来越被迫妥善处理并发性。 Java 语言从一开始就包含了对并发的支持，尽管犯了一些错误，后来必须在多个版本中进行纠正，以便更正确、更高效地进行并发编程。 C++ 语言长期以来一直被用来编写重型多线程系统，但它根本没有对并发的标准化支持（ISO C++ 标准甚至没有提到线程，并且是故意这样做的），因此通常必须通过使用不可移植的特定于平台的并发功能和库来实现并发。 （它通常也是不完整的；例如，静态变量只能初始化一次，这通常要求编译器用锁包装它们，但许多 C++ 实现不会生成锁。） 最后，还有一些并发标准，包括 pthreads 和 OpenMP，其中一些标准支持隐式和显式并行化。 让编译器查看您的单线程程序并自动找出如何隐式并行化它是很好的，但这些自动转换工具是有限的，并且不会产生您自己编写的显式并发控制的收益。 主流的技术水平围绕基于锁的编程，这是微妙且危险的。 我们迫切需要比当今语言提供的更高级别的并发编程模型；我很快就会对此有更多内容要说。结论如果您还没有这样做，那么现在是时候仔细检查应用程序的设计，确定哪些操作现在或可能很快变得对 CPU 敏感，并确定这些地方如何从并发中受益。 现在也是您和您的团队了解并发编程的要求、陷阱、风格和习惯用法的时候了。少数罕见的应用程序类别自然是可并行的，但大多数都不是。 即使您确切地知道哪里受 CPU 限制，您也可能会发现很难弄清楚如何并行化这些操作；现在就开始考虑这个问题是最有理由的。 隐式并行编译器可以提供一点帮助，但不要期望太多；它们无法像通过将顺序程序转变为显式并行和线程版本那样出色地并行化顺序程序。由于缓存的持续增长以及可能更多的增量直线控制流优化，免费午餐将持续一段时间；但从今天开始，自助餐将只提供一份主菜和一份甜点。 吞吐量增益的菲力牛排仍然在菜单上，但现在它需要额外的开发工作、额外的代码复杂性和额外的测试工作。 好消息是，对于许多类别的应用程序来说，额外的努力是值得的，因为并发性将使它们充分利用处理器吞吐量的持续指数增长。
